title: Ephemeral Egress Window Prioritizer & Upgrade Runway Intake
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customers requesting Private/VPC/on-prem deployments frequently surface two related blockers: (1) narrow, timeboxed egress windows for upgrades/patches and (2) requirement for scheduled maintenance runway aligned to their change control. Current intake captures these as free-text tickets and routing to SEs is ad-hoc, causing long cycles and inconsistent SLAs. This ticket defines a structured intake fragment and prioritization rubric to capture ephemeral egress constraints, weekend/maintenance windows, rollback expectations, and business-critical upgrade runway. The objective is to standardize scoring, speed up routing to engineering or concierge onboarding lanes, and enable predictable SLAs for customers with tight networking restrictions.
acceptance_criteria: Create a 7-field intake form fragment to be embedded in the self-serve and concierge intake: egress_windows, allowed_ips, maintenance_timezone, blackout_dates, expected_patch_duration_mins, rollback_tolerance, escalation_contact
Define a weighted prioritization rubric (score 0-100) that includes business criticality, blast radius, customer maturity, automation readiness, and legal/compliance constraints
Add routing rules: score >= 80 -> fasttrack concierge lane; score 50-79 -> engineering triage + 3 business day SLA; score <50 -> standard backlog
Document handoff playbook for SE -> Eng -> Concierge including required artifacts (network runbook, patch playbook, signed maintenance window)
Create dashboard in Console showing intake volume, average time-to-schedule, and top network blockers within 4 weeks
Pilot intake with three enterprise customers and measure time-to-approved-window reduction by >= 30%
Security review flag present on intake when egress policy requires temporary keying/KMS access
comments: 2025-02-19: Initial problem framing with PM + Solutions Eng; collected 5 recent customer requests and measured median time-to-approve = 16 days (notes in Confluence). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Egress+Window+Study

2025-02-22: Engineering scoping sync: ENG identified two major constraints — (a) automation to open/close egress via bastion/proxy and (b) upgrade orchestration calendar. Eng proposed a small API to accept scheduled windows (PRD link below).

2025-02-25: Design review: DES recommended micro-copy to reduce ambiguous answers in intake (eg. clarify timezone format and required CIDR notation). UX mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/egress-intake-v1.png

2025-03-01: Decided to include a temporary 'escrowed-egress' checkbox for legal signoff cases; security signoff required when checked — flagged security_review_required=true. Logged dependency on ENG-49102 for calendar API and ENG-50218 for bastion automation.

2025-03-04: Draft rubric shared with GTM and CS — received feedback to weight 'customer business criticality' higher for top-tier accounts. Updated scoring weights in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Egress+Prioritization+Rubric
2025-03-05: Kickoff pilot with three customers scheduled; onboarding checklist and playbook PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-intake/pull/142
notes: Trade-offs discussed: creating too many 'fasttrack' buckets increases operational load; aim for clear routing and automation where possible.
Fallback plan: if bastion automation delayed, concierge will operate with pre-signed temporary VPN tokens and manual closed window logging
Measure success via: (a) median days-to-approved-window, (b) % of escalations to SEs, (c) pilot customer NPS on onboarding
